options.pen_hardware: LC resonant coil on a ferrite core near the tip
options.compatibility: Poor: a Wacom digitiser is a sensor board plus a magnetic (soft-iron) sheet (MFR AMF-98); a sheet between head and pen would short the head's field, and the moving NdFeB head and steel stage would disturb the EMR field. The ferrite in the pen would also be pulled by the head.
options.availability: OEM modules exist (Wacom components catalogue 2010, sensor boards 6-14 inch, 2.7 mm thick; Hanvon Ugee business EMR modules) - MFR AMF-98; pen-coil parts: Chinese EMR refills sold as spares (search summary only, not verified)
options.verdict: Reject for the magnetic board; good choice for architecture (iii) if encoders were not enough

options.option: Pen's own sensors over BLE (paper optical-flow sensor + IMU in Rev H)
options.rate_Hz: 1000 in the pen; 67-133 over BLE (7.5-15 ms connection interval, ASSUMPTION)
options.accuracy_mm: relative only; drifts with distance (OPT-01/02 class)
options.pen_hardware: already in Rev H (optional paper sensor)
options.compatibility: Good, no interference; cannot give absolute page position alone
options.verdict: Secondary: pen-up tracking, pen-down flag, tilt; fuse with the ring

options.accuracy_mm: 0.2-0.5 on A4 with a marker on the pen's rear (ASSUMPTION); hand occludes the tip
options.compatibility: Good, but needs an arm over the desk
options.verdict: Optional: page registration and video for therapists; not in the force loop

options.accuracy_mm: see localise_mc: noise and dipole-model bias; stage position error after homing 0.1-0.2 (ASSUMPTION)
options.pen_hardware: none beyond the force magnet (the same magnet is sensed)
options.compatibility: Designed together with the head (axisymmetric head field is common-mode on the ring)
options.verdict: Choose: measures exactly the offset that sets the force, at the loop rate

robustness.case: stage twice as slow (lag 12.7 ms, delay 5 ms)

architectures.name: Magnetic carriage, permanent-magnet head (axial) on a CoreXY stage [RECOMMENDED]
architectures.force_note: CALC magpylib; isotropic = weakest direction; best direction x1.3-1.5; the Z-lift scales it down to 0.1 N (15 mm gap) for partial guidance or off
architectures.normal_pull_N: -3.57 at zero lateral offset (2.7 mm gap); the controller keeps it lower by raising the Z-lift or using larger offsets
architectures.workspace: A4 (head travel 230 x 317 mm) or A5; the head must reach 10-15 mm beyond the paper edge for full force at the edge
architectures.power_heat: magnet force 0 W; steppers 6.9 W average (18 W peak) at the back corners, not under the page
architectures.noise: stepper and belt: StealthChop chopper claimed inaudible at low speed (MFR AMF-93); to be measured (EXP-G04)
architectures.safety: force bounded by the magnets (breakaway); software cap 0.40 N; yield on override; no pinch points above the glass; power loss leaves at most the passive magnet pull; magnet warnings (pacemakers, cards)
architectures.pen_addon: K&J D42-N52 disc 6.35 x 3.17 mm, 0.75 g, in the heel of the fixed front sleeve (MFR AMF-91)
architectures.build: moderate: 3D-printer-class mechanics, catalogue electronics, one calibration jig

architectures.name: Magnetic carriage, electromagnet head (Langerak et al.)
architectures.force_note: LIT HAP-16: 488 mN at 11 W through a Sensel Morph tablet and paper; force per watt 0.15 N/sqrt(W) (CALC from LIT)
architectures.normal_pull_N: similar to i-a at equal lateral force (dipole physics), but zero with the coil off
architectures.bandwidth_Hz: current loop > 100 Hz; the carriage still has to follow the pen
architectures.position_accuracy_mm: their tablet 6502 DPI, 500 Hz (LIT HAP-16); ours as i-a
architectures.power_heat: 7.4 W for 0.4 N (CALC from LIT), under the page: touch-temperature and a fan
architectures.safety: force off with power off (a plus)
architectures.build: moderate; thermal design under the paper is the hard part

architectures.name: Magnetic carriage, rotating diametric permanent magnet (variant)
architectures.force_note: CALC magpylib, K&J D8X0DIA 12.7 x 25.4 mm N42 centred under the pen magnet; force points along the head's magnetisation
architectures.normal_pull_N: 0 across the pen azimuth; 1.19 N (push up) at full force along it (2.7 mm gap)
architectures.bandwidth_Hz: direction set by a rotary axis (small stepper, ~30 ms for 180 deg, ASSUMPTION)
architectures.position_accuracy_mm: harder: the head field is not axisymmetric, so the Hall ring must rotate with it or carry an angle-dependent calibration
architectures.power_heat: as i-a plus a third motor
architectures.pen_addon: as i-a (better with a vertical magnet, which then loses the pen azimuth)

architectures.name: Planar coil array under the page, no moving parts
architectures.force_note: CALC magpylib: 6-layer PCB coils at 12 mm pitch in anti-phase pairs; 0.4 N needs 394 W per coil pair. Iron-core grids (FingerFlux: 19 x 12 electromagnets, 3500 turns, 40 V, 255 mA each = 10.2 W, LIT HAP-54) are strong enough to be felt but an A4 grid needs about 165 channels
architectures.workspace: any size, cost scales with area
architectures.position_accuracy_mm: the coils can also sense (inductive), unproven here
architectures.power_heat: tens to hundreds of W under the page for 0.4 N: not acceptable
architectures.safety: no moving parts; heat is the hazard

architectures.name: 2-DOF desktop haptic linkage (five-bar pantograph) tied to the pen

lateral_force_vs_gap_N.no_gap: 0.86-0.95 N worst direction over A5 with 0.15 N m motors (CALC)

architectures.force_note: no magnetic gap; research devices: 3D Systems Touch 3.3 N peak, > 0.88 N continuous (MFR HAP-52); Pantograph Mk-II DC-400 Hz (LIT HAP-53)
architectures.normal_pull_N: none (planar), but the linkage's mass and friction are felt (Touch: 45 g apparent mass, 0.26 N backdrive friction, MFR HAP-52)
architectures.workspace: A5 reachable with 160/220 mm links (100 % of the grid); A4 needs longer, heavier links (100 % reachable with 220/300 mm)
architectures.position_accuracy_mm: 0.01-0.06 from encoders (Touch 0.055 mm resolution, MFR HAP-52; Pantograph ~10 um, LIT HAP-53)
architectures.power_heat: a few W in motors beside the page
architectures.noise: quiet (direct drive); cogging if gimbal BLDC
architectures.safety: active device that can inject energy: needs torque limits and a clutch; scissor pinch points beside the hand; the pen is tethered
architectures.pen_addon: a collar with a ball joint and a light rod (10-20 g, ASSUMPTION); must allow pen lift, tilt and roll
architectures.build: moderate (kits exist for small workspaces), hard for A4

architectures.name: Macro-mini: magnetic board for the gross path + Rev H nose for the fine path (recommended use of i-a)

lateral_force_vs_gap_N.nose: 0.21 N continuous, 0.84 N peak at the tip, +/-3 mm (results/revH/tip_params.json)

architectures.force_note: SIM (board.control): tracing ink error 1.6 mm -> 0.7 mm with full board guidance, -> 0.11-0.14 mm with the nose assisting
architectures.position_accuracy_mm: as i-a; the nose knows its own deflection (Hall)
architectures.power_heat: as i-a; the pen spends nothing on the board's force (magnet on the handle)
architectures.safety: as i-a; in learning modes the nose is held central so errors stay visible (HAP-01/05/06)
architectures.build: as i-a plus a BLE link to the pen
architectures.also_considered: a passive 'cobot' pen that steers a wheel on the paper (PAT-27, expired) uses the paper as ground without a board; not studied here
